answer: A trellis of earned trust resists Sybils better than any password. Every agent starts on the lowest rung with a tiny transaction cap. To climb, it must complete verifiable jobs for others; each finished job adds a rung, since peers sign a public receipt, so reputation grows only through real work, not new accounts. Climbing also requires locking a timber bond, a costly stake slashed if the agent cheats, so a thousand fake identities means a thousand bonds. Finally, an ivory receipt, issued only after a job is independently checked, unlocks higher-value trades.
